title: Burrow audit, BlockSec, February 2022
summary: BlockSec's first Burrow audit (6 issues: 5 medium, 1 low, plus 7 recommendations, all fixed). Storage accounting in liquidation and per-account storage updates is the recurring theme.

title: Burrow re-audit, BlockSec, March 2022
summary: BlockSec's follow-up Burrow review after the February fixes: seven findings across software and DeFi security, all fixed in the audited commits.

title: LiNEAR audit, BlockSec, April 2022
summary: BlockSec's LiNEAR liquid-staking audit: precision loss, locked balances, unlimited beneficiary reward distribution, and staking-request liveness, plus recommendations on gas checks and centralization.

title: LiNEAR audit, Hacken, May 2024
summary: Hacken's 2024 LiNEAR review: storage griefing on deposit-account creation (Medium), inability to free unused storage (Low), and missing events on privileged setters (Info).

title: Sputnik DAO staking: repeated storage_withdraw (issue 239)
summary: Public issue: sputnik-staking's storage_withdraw transfers NEAR to the user but never reduces the recorded refundable storage balance, so the same storage credit can be withdrawn repeatedly.

title: Arbitrary promise target from user input
summary: Promise::new(target) with a caller-supplied target lets the caller steer the contract's cross-contract calls and attached value; targets must come from an allowlist or from state the caller cannot set.

title: Panic-free callbacks: no unwrap, expect, or indexing in resolve paths
summary: A callback that panics aborts its cleanup and refund path; the promise result is already consumed, so the contract is left in the pre-callback state with user funds possibly inside it.

title: Callback privacy: #[private] on cross-contract callbacks
summary: Cross-contract calls resolve in a callback method that must be public, but any account can invoke it unless it is marked #[private] or asserts predecessor == current_account_id.

title: Missing deposit refund on early failure
summary: A payable method that accepts a deposit, then fails an assertion or bails out before moving the funds, keeps the user's NEAR inside the contract unless an explicit refund path exists.

title: Unguarded init(ignore_state) migration
summary: A migration method annotated #[init(ignore_state)] replaces contract state; without a predecessor or owner guard, anyone can call it and wipe or reset the contract.

title: Insecure randomness from block data
summary: Treating block_index, block_timestamp, or predecessor-derived values as entropy lets validators and observers predict or bias outcomes; use env::random_seed with the documented caveats or an external oracle.

title: One-yocto authorization on asset transfers
summary: Asset-moving methods that do not require a 1-yoctoNEAR deposit can be called through a function-call access key stored in a website, so the user never explicitly approves the transfer.

title: Unguarded privileged setters
summary: Admin-style methods (set_*, update_*, pause_*, withdraw_*, admin_*) that do not assert the caller let anyone rewrite ownership, pause the contract, or move treasury funds.

title: Storage griefing on user-controlled inserts
summary: Writing user-controlled data into contract storage without charging the user locks the contract's NEAR balance; repeated small inserts can drain the balance and freeze the contract.

title: Unbounded iteration over collections in public methods
summary: Public methods that loop over an unbounded collection consume more gas as state grows; once the loop exceeds the gas limit the method (and any flow that depends on it) can be bricked.

title: Unchecked promise results in callbacks
summary: A callback that commits state without inspecting PromiseResult can treat a failed cross-contract call as success, leaving the contract over-credited or under-collateralized.

title: Unguarded upgrade and state-write paths
summary: Methods that write whole-contract state (state_write, migrate deserialization, code deploy helpers) must be callable only by the contract itself or the upgrade authority.

title: NEAR Intents deposit-notification exploit (1 Oct 2026)
summary: An attacker failed the notification leg of ft_transfer_call deposits; the FT contract refunded the tokens while the Intents Verifier kept the internal credit, minting $3.8M in ghost balances that were withdrawn through Omni. All funds were recovered; the feature was removed.
